messages.content: Implement a Python function from a JSON behavioral card. The card is the only task specification. Return a JSON object with a single string field code containing executable Python source. Define solve with the card's exact signature. Use only Python's standard library. Allowed imports: math, itertools, functools, collections, heapq, bisect, statistics, fractions, operator, typing. Do not import or call NumPy, SymPy, NetworkX or any other third-party library. Do not read files, use network, introspection, eval, exec, input or print. Implement computations yourself using built-ins and the allowed standard library. Return plain JSON-compatible values, not iterators or sets; use string keys in dictionaries. Include any helper functions in the code. No tests or main block. Raise ValueError where the card requires it.

Implement this card:
{
  "algorithm": [
    "Check if the graph can be colored with two colors such that no two adjacent vertices share the same color.",
    "Perform a BFS or DFS traversal starting from an arbitrary vertex, assigning alternating colors (0 and 1).",
    "If during traversal, an adjacent vertex has the same color as the current vertex, the graph is not bipartite.",
    "If all vertices are colored without conflicts, the graph is bipartite."
  ],
  "constraints": [
    "n is an integer >= : 1",
    "edges contains distinct pairs with 0<=u<v<n",
    "Graph is simple and undirected",
    "Vertices are labeled 0 to n-1"
  ],
  "edge_cases": [
    "Graph with a single vertex (n=1) is bipartite.",
    "Graph with no edges (n vertices) is bipartite.",
    "Graph with an odd-length cycle is not bipartite.",
    "Graph with multiple connected components: each component must be bipartite for the entire graph to be bipartite."
  ],
  "inputs": "n (integer >= 1) and edges (list of distinct [u,v] pairs where 0<=u<v<n)",
  "method_id": "networkx.is_bipartite",
  "output": "True if the graph is bipartite, False otherwise",
  "purpose": "Determine if a simple undirected graph with n vertices (labeled 0 to n-1) and given edges is bipartite.",
  "signature": "solve(n, edges)"
}
